title: On perfect matchings, edge-colourings and eigenvalues of cubic graphs: spectral characterisation of truncated cubic graphs (Proposition 3)
author: Willem H. Haemers
work: On perfect matchings, edge-colourings and eigenvalues of cubic graphs
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition 3 (source0.tex lines 177--179), "Being a truncated cubic graph is a property characterised by the spectrum", delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 181--192 (12 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The proposition asserts that the class of truncated cubic graphs is spectrally determined, and the proof is a genuine spectral-reconstruction argument: from the spectrum of T(G) one first recovers the order 3n and the presence of n triangles, then uses the spectral invariance of the number of closed 4-walks together with the fact that T(G) has no 4-cycles and hence only trivial closed 4-walks, to force H to have no 4-cycles either; that in turn forces the triangles of H to be pairwise disjoint and any two triangles to share at most one edge, after which the graph G' on the triangles, with adjacency inherited from H, satisfies H=T(G'). Each of those steps is a distinct mathematical move (spectral invariants, walk counting, cycle structure, reconstruction of a cubic graph from its triangle system), not an unpacking of definitions, and the result is a new spectral characterisation rather than a restatement of the truncation construction. H2: a complete original research-paper proposition, short but with a real multi-step argument whose two nontrivial steps (closed 4-walk counting and the triangle-system reconstruction) are not qualifying-exam material.
